All 7 explored fully — home, about, easter eggs, fonts, colors, stacks, interactions. Screenshots broken (headless CDP), so used text + computed styles + DOM inspection instead. Full report:

# The 7 — what each one is

| Site | Stack | Vibe |
|---|---|---|
| eftakher.me | Framer | dark, serif display (Bluu Next) + mono accents, light/dark toggle |
| ericsin.com | Framer | light, Exposure serif + Fragment Mono, playful |
| dai.is-a.dev | Next.js (open source) | dark "Vercel UI", IBM Plex Serif + Geist, ⌘K palette |
| pablostanley.com | custom | near-black, DM Sans, one long list page |
| pham.codes | custom | light, Geist Mono only, all-lowercase, ASCII portrait |
| loganliffick.com | Next.js | ultra-minimal Inter, one screen |
| evilrabbit.com | v0 | pure black, Geist Sans, pure timeline |

# What's common — the pattern you respond to

**1. Typography IS the design.** Every one uses tiny font stack (often 1 family), and type carries layout. Mono fonts everywhere (Geist Mono, Fragment Mono) = design-engineer aesthetic. Zero stock-looking typography.

**2. Radical restraint.** Solid black or white bg, ~zero color, no gradients, no generic SaaS cards. Pablo/Logan/Evil Rabbit/Pham = almost text documents. Confidence through omission.

**3. Zero throat-clearing.** No "Welcome to my website". One line identity → straight to work. Evil Rabbit = 2 sentences then career table. Pham = "today / past / links". They treat your attention as expensive.

**4. Career as timeline + years.** Vercel 2016-, AuditBoard 2022, Freelance 1998–2006. Scannable, humble, no story-bloat.

**5. Receipts, not claims.** Metrics everywhere: "$9.1M in sales", "189% more productive", "30k weekly downloads", GitHub stars + contribution graph, Awwwards link, Outerbase link → Cloudflare acquisition press release. Social proof from named famous people (Guillermo Rauch, shadcn, Evil Rabbit praising Dai's work).

**6. Personality artifacts / easter eggs** — this is the big one:
- Eric: "Kitties Adopted" stat stuck at 0, "most proud of my two kitties and my wife"
- Logan: stealth project named `▓▓▒░▒▒░` blocks, secret /workspace desk-photos page, email copy toast
- Pablo: "Yoink any video. No shady ads", "Un abrazote" sign-off
- Pham: face rendered as ASCII art, refuses capital letters
- Dai: `FIG_001` label, "Good morning" (time-aware), live local clock + timezone + phone + pronouns
- Eftakher: nomadic coffee life photos, live Madrid clock

**7. Honest availability.** "Open to opportunities", "Unavailable for freelance until Q2 2026", "send a dm". No fake scarcity, no "Contact me" corporate page.

**8. Small interactive toys.** ⌘K command palette, count-up stats, copy-to-clipboard, theme toggle, marquee. One or two — never a fireworks show. Craft proven through details, not through hero animation.

**9. The site itself is the portfolio.** Mostly hand-built (Next.js/v0) or Framer, several open-source or Awwwards-winning. They break conventions on purpose (lowercase, ASCII face, censored project names, essay titled "You shouldn't become a designer").

# Why you liked them so much

You = developer who cares about design. These sites are all **"design engineer" energy** — Vercel-orbit taste (3 of 7 literally work at Vercel). Common formula:

```
restraint + strong type + receipts + one weird personal detail
```

They feel **handmade by a person with opinions**, not generated for a client. They prove skill through small perfect details (a toast, a clock, a ⌘K palette) instead of shouting through huge visuals. And every one hides humor/easter eggs that reward a builder who inspects the site — that's you. You liked them because browsing them feels like finding the source code, not reading a landing page.

Translation for your portfolio: black or white bg, one great mono + one serif/sans pairing, identity in one line, work as timeline with years, 3–5 real metrics, one easter egg, one interactive toy, availability badge, done.

7: **Portfolio**:

9: _Avoid_: Product site, marketing site, blog-only, side project dump

11: **Visitor**:
12: An engineer, recruiter, or hiring engineer evaluating Dhruv’s credibility.
13: _Avoid_: User, customer, reader (unless specifically reading a Post)
14: 
15: **AI-pilled**:
16: Default identity as “the AI person” — builds and thinks with AI/agents as the primary way of working, not as a side interest.
17: _Avoid_: AI-curious, uses ChatGPT, ML researcher (unless a Post is specifically about that)
18: 
19: **Design Engineer**:
20: Someone who ships interface craft at a high bar — design and frontend are the same job, not separate handoffs. The Portfolio itself is evidence of this.
21: _Avoid_: Frontend developer, UI designer, “I also do design”
22: 
23: **Product thinking**:
24: Clear judgment about what to build, why, and where it fits — shown primarily through writing, not slogans.
25: _Avoid_: Product manager, strategist, “visionary”
26: 
27: **Editorial surface**:
28: The Portfolio’s visual and UX north star — warm monochrome editorial craft in the lineage of pablostanley.com / loganliffick.com / evilrabbit.com: warm-tinted neutrals (never cool gray), hairline-divided CV rows (name → one-line description → url ↗ → year/date), 12px uppercase micro-labels with wide tracking, Geist type and spacing doing the work. No chromatic accent in chrome; blue survives only inside the AI Activity heatmap. Flat background — no gradients, no noise. Light is the primary theme; a polished warm dark theme is also available. Motion stays quiet and intentional (theme transition, hovers, heatmap tooltip, staggered fade-rise entrances) — craft through restraint, not spectacle. Signature details: inverted-ink text selection and a live local-time readout in the footer.
29: _Avoid_: Dashboard-first, marketing-campaign, “SaaS admin UI”, dark-only, scroll-jacking, particle heroes, atmospheric gradients/noise, colored accents outside the heatmap
30: 
31: **AI Activity**:
32: A GitHub-contribution-style heatmap of Dhruv’s AI usage on Home under the profile/intro. Year grid of day cells (intensity by tokens), hover tooltip (date + tokens), quiet legend, plus a single lifetime-tokens summary. Fixture data until ingestion exists. Reference image was conceptual only — no Daily/Weekly/Cumulative tabs or streak/analytics chrome in v1.
33: _Avoid_: Analytics dashboard, Observability, “stats section”, copying a specific product’s chrome
34: 
35: **Home**:
36: The landing surface. One centered 42rem column for everything — header, sections, footer. Section order: profile/intro → AI Activity → selected Projects → latest Writings (only if at least one Post is published) → footer. Primary nav destination. The intro is a short rewritten editorial block (name + brief positioning + pulsing status line + mono socials row) — not the old bio, and not omitted. Sections separate by whitespace (~64px) only; hairlines belong to lists, not section boundaries. Footer is minimal (name/©, live local time, mono socials + RSS); no mega-footer.
37: _Avoid_: Landing page, dashboard, feed, slogan stacks, long About essay on Home, empty Writings teaser on Home, section divider lines, sticky/blurred header chrome
38: 
39: **Writings**:
40: The writing index and articles — where Product thinking is proven. Nav label and routes are **Writings**: `/writings` and `/writings/[slug]`. RSS at `/feed.xml` (head/footer discovery, not primary nav). At first ship there may be zero published Posts — the surface still exists with a quiet empty/coming-soon state; MDX pipeline, RSS, and SEO stay wired for when Posts land.
41: _Avoid_: Blog, Articles, Journal, Newsletter, `/blog` as the public path, fake sample essays presented as real
42: 
43: **Post**:
44: One piece of writing under Writings. MDX body with frontmatter: title, published date, summary, optional tags; slug from the file path. Drafts exist but never ship publicly. Reading time may be derived; no view counters, reactions, or multi-author in v1.
45: _Avoid_: Article, essay, blog post (in UI copy prefer Post/Writings)
46: 
47: **Projects**:
48: The project index — shipped work as proof. Presented as an editorial, text-only list; links outbound to repo or demo. Each Project has name, one-line description, url, optional year, and optional selected flag for Home. No thumbnails, cards, tag chips, or project detail pages in v1.
49: _Avoid_: Work, Portfolio items, Case studies (unless a specific Post is a case study), template marketplace grid

51: **Primary nav**:
52: Exactly three items: Home, Writings, Projects. RSS exists as a feed URL, not a nav item. Header also includes a quiet theme control (Vercel-like) that follows system preference by default and persists a manual override. The header is non-sticky and un-chromed: no border, no blur, same 42rem column as content.

3:  * Public-safe: daily combined token totals only.

5: export type AiActivityPayload = {
6:   version: 1;
7:   generatedAt: string;
8:   timezone: string;
9:   /** Complete days only (through yesterday in `timezone`). */
10:   days: { date: string; tokens: number }[];
11:   lifetimeTokens: number;
12: };

14: export const AI_ACTIVITY_TIMEZONE = "Asia/Kolkata";
15: export const AI_ACTIVITY_BLOB_PATH = "ai-activity/latest.json";
16: export const AI_ACTIVITY_MAX_DAYS = 800;
17: const MAX_GENERATED_AT_LEN = 40;
18: const MAX_TIMEZONE_LEN = 64;
19: 
20: export function isValidIanaTimeZone(timeZone: string): boolean {
21:   if (
22:     timeZone.length < 1 ||
23:     timeZone.length > MAX_TIMEZONE_LEN ||
24:     timeZone !== timeZone.trim()
25:   ) {
26:     return false;
27:   }
28:   try {
29:     Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone });
30:     return true;
31:   } catch {
32:     return false;
33:   }
34: }

36: export function isAiActivityPayload(value: unknown): value is AiActivityPayload {
37:   if (!value || typeof value !== "object") return false;
38:   const v = value as Record<string, unknown>;
39:   if (v.version !== 1) return false;
40:   if (
41:     typeof v.generatedAt !== "string" ||
42:     v.generatedAt.length === 0 ||
43:     v.generatedAt.length > MAX_GENERATED_AT_LEN
44:   ) {
45:     return false;
46:   }
47:   if (typeof v.timezone !== "string" || !isValidIanaTimeZone(v.timezone)) {
48:     return false;
49:   }
50:   if (
51:     typeof v.lifetimeTokens !== "number" ||
52:     !Number.isFinite(v.lifetimeTokens) ||
53:     v.lifetimeTokens < 0
54:   ) {
55:     return false;

40: const ENV_FILE = join(STATE_DIR, "env");

42: function loadEnvFile(path: string) {
43:   if (!existsSync(path)) return;
44:   for (const line of readFileSync(path, "utf8").split("\n")) {
45:     const trimmed = line.trim();
46:     if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith("#")) continue;
47:     const eq = trimmed.indexOf("=");
48:     if (eq < 0) continue;
49:     const key = trimmed.slice(0, eq).trim();
50:     const value = trimmed.slice(eq + 1).trim();
51:     if (!(key in process.env) || process.env[key] === "") {
52:       process.env[key] = value;
53:     }
54:   }
55: }

59: const TIMEZONE = process.env.AI_ACTIVITY_TIMEZONE ?? AI_ACTIVITY_TIMEZONE;
60: const parsedStale = Number(process.env.AI_ACTIVITY_STALE_HOURS ?? 26);
61: const STALE_HOURS =
62:   Number.isFinite(parsedStale) && parsedStale > 0 ? parsedStale : 26;
63: const FORCE = process.env.AI_ACTIVITY_FORCE === "1";
64: const INGEST_URL = process.env.AI_ACTIVITY_INGEST_URL;

90:   writeFileSync(tmp, `${JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)}\n`);
91:   renameSync(tmp, path);

## Stack (greenfield, ADR-0003)
Next.js 16.2.10 + React 19 + Tailwind v4 + TypeScript, bun-managed. Geist Sans + Mono. Motion for entrances, next-themes, MDX (next-mdx-remote + sugar-high + sanitize), @vercel/blob, Analytics + Speed Insights. 50 tests across 13 files — all pass. Branch `feat/warm-mono-redesign`, 15 commits.

## Design system (already in the 7-site lineage)
Warm stone monochrome (`#fafaf9` light / `#131312` dark), one 42rem column for everything, hairline CV rows, 12px uppercase tracking-[0.2em] micro-labels, inverted-ink selection, zero accents except heatmap blue. Quiet motion: 0.55s expo staggered fade-rise, all reduced-motion safe. CONTEXT.md explicitly cites pablostanley/loganliffick/evilrabbit as north star.

## Features inventory

| Feature | State |
|---|---|
| **AI Activity heatmap** | Flagship. GitHub-style year grid of daily AI tokens |
| Token pipeline | tokscale → nightly LaunchAgent sync → Bearer-auth ingest API → Vercel Blob → ISR (1h) → fallback JSON |
| Live-today cell | Synthetic projection (7-day min baseline × % of day elapsed), 90s eased count-up, min-interval refresh |
| Heatmap UX | Hover tooltip footer w/ live count, Less/More legend, a11y labels, mobile scroll |
| **Home** | intro → AI Activity → Selected Projects → Writings (conditional sections) |
| Intro | Name + positioning + pulsing status dot ("Under development. Waiting for Kimi K3 open-weights") + mono socials |
| **Projects** | 8 hardcoded, 5 selected w/ homeRank order. CV rows: name → desc → url ↗ → year (years empty) |
| **Writings** | MDX pipeline, frontmatter + drafts, reading time, anchor headings, safe-link policy, 1 test Post |
| **Chrome** | Non-sticky header (logo mark + 3-item nav + theme toggle), footer w/ live local clock + socials + RSS |
| **SEO** | Dynamic OG image route, JSON-LD (WebSite/Person + BlogPosting), sitemap, robots, RSS `/feed.xml` |
| **A11y** | skip link, aria-current, reduced motion, keyboard-reachable cells |

## Live state (verified just now)
Site runs, heatmap shows **6,957,491,873 lifetime tokens** — real blob data flowing. All 3 pages + post + RSS render clean.

# Gaps vs the 7 you love

1. **No career timeline w/ years** — their backbone. Yours has none (no experience anywhere).
2. **Project years missing** — rows support it, data empty.
3. **No About/story** — Pablo has "Now / Before / About", Eric has journey page.
4. **Availability note is joke-status, not hiring signal** — "waiting for K3 weights" is fun; theirs say open/unavailable for work.
5. **Zero easter eggs** beyond status note — no ⌘K, no ASCII, no stealth-blocks moment.
6. Testimonials/social-proof wall — Dai has one, you have token numbers (arguably better).

# Questions

1. **Projects real vs placeholder names** — are all 8 repos public + final names? Should years be populated (they render already)?
2. **Experience section** — want a Work/Experience timeline like theirs, or stay projects-only?
3. **About page** — yes/no? Or keep Home sparse per CONTEXT.md ("no long About essay on Home")?
4. **Ship-blocker** — status note says waiting for Kimi K3 weights; that's literally tonight/week? Or placeholder joke that needs replacing before launch?
5. **Writings** — is the test Post staying until first real essay? Any essays already written elsewhere to port?
6. **Domain** — is dhruv2mars.com already deployed w/ blob live, or pre-launch everything?

Answer what matters, then we plan next moves.
